questions.q: What problem does a config dictionary or config file solve for this pipeline?
options: It makes the script run faster
It separates what the pipeline does from which files and settings it's pointed at, so those can change without editing the code
It removes the need for any functions at all
It encrypts the source data automatically
questions.explain: Config-driven design means changing a file path or table name doesn't require touching the pipeline's logic.

questions.q: What does load_config() do in this lesson's script?
options: It reads config.json and returns it as a Python dictionary
It connects directly to AdventureWorks2012
It deletes the watermark file
It validates the orders.csv data
questions.explain: load_config() uses json.load() to turn the config file into a dictionary the rest of the script uses.

questions.q: Which earlier lesson's technique does load_upsert() in this script rely on to avoid duplicate rows?
options: Lesson 29's parameterized queries only
Lesson 37's INSERT OR REPLACE upsert pattern, keyed on order_id
Lesson 30's SQLAlchemy engine
Lesson 26's connection string
questions.explain: The script reuses Lesson 37's upsert pattern so reruns don't create duplicate rows.

questions.q: What is main()'s role in this lesson's script?
options: It defines the CONFIG dictionary values directly
It is the script's single entry point: load the config, then run the pipeline, catching and re-raising any failure
It only prints the config file's contents
It replaces the need for run_pipeline() entirely
questions.explain: main() ties configuration loading and pipeline execution together as the script's one entry point.

questions.q: What happens if run_pipeline() finds no rows newer than the current watermark?
options: It raises an error and stops the script
It deletes the existing warehouse table
It prints that there are no new rows and returns without writing anything
It reloads the entire dataset from scratch regardless
questions.explain: An empty incremental extract means nothing needs loading, so the function exits early with a message.
